anna_cs: Hey team — acme-analytics reported a regression after last night's model swap. Same query + candidate list yields very different rerank scores (and user-facing order) compared to yesterday. Attaching minimal repro below.

raj_dev: Can you paste the exact request body you sent? Also which model id did we promote?

anna_cs: Model promoted: text-rerank-v2-2026-03-16 (deploy tag: canary->prod). Payload: ```json
{
  "query": "best office coffee machine",
  "candidates": ["cheap brewer", "gourmet espresso", "single serve pod"],
  "top_k": 0,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```
Expected top score for "gourmet espresso" ~0.92 (yesterday). Observed top score now is "cheap brewer" 0.87, "gourmet espresso" drops to 0.65. Customer saw large UX churn.

maria_research: Interesting. Any chance tokenization changed? Trailing whitespace or control chars can flip rerank. Can you confirm raw bytes of the query?

anna_cs: Raw query bytes: `62 65 73 74 20 6f 66 66 69 63 65 20 63 6f 66 66 65 65 20 6d 61 63 68 69 6e 65` (no weird chars). I also tried adding explicit `
` and got slightly different scores but still the order flipped.

jordan_infra: Deploy-bot shows the rollout completed at 03:12 UTC, but we kept canary traffic at 10% for 30m. No infra errors in that window. I can confirm prod and canary are running same container image, but runtime flags differed: `--kv-cache=on` enabled in prod. Could KV-caching affect rerank outputs?

raj_dev: KV cache should be deterministic for scoring-only endpoints, but if we accidentally enabled a tokenization shim or a post-tokenize normalization patch in the new runtime, that could change model inputs. Maria: any model-side changes in the onboarding?

maria_research: We released a micro-patch to the tokenizer to normalize curly quotes in a downstream pipeline (intended to reduce token growth). It landed in the model build used yesterday for canary, but prod image got the patched tokenization at rollout time. That mismatch could explain it.

anna_cs: Repro steps I gave to customer (short):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d "<payload above>"
2) set `temperature:0.0`, `top_k:0`, and `normalize_punctuation:false` vs true
3) compare scores.

raj_dev: I ran the exact payload against both model versions locally. With old tokenizer: scores = ["gourmet espresso":0.91, "cheap brewer":0.72, "single serve pod":0.45]. With patched tokenizer: scores = ["cheap brewer":0.87, "gourmet espresso":0.65, "single serve pod":0.48]. So it's the tokenizer change.

maria_research: That matches my hypothesis. It looks like punctuation normalization merged some tokens in the candidate text, changing relative likelihoods. Not a model weight issue.

anna_cs: Customer wants rollback or mitigation. They have strict ordering guarantees. Any quick mitigations we can offer (short of full rollback)?

jordan_infra: Short-term: we can route acme-analytics traffic to a cluster running the previous tokenizer-enabled image (same model weights) — create a routing override for their org id. I'll prepare a canary route.

raj_dev: Medium-term: add a deterministic tokenization flag to the rerank API (e.g., `tokenizer_profile: legacy|normalized`) so customers can pin behavior. Also add a release-note/onboarding checklist so tokenizer patches can't silently change semantics.

maria_research: I'll open a regression ticket with patch diff and tests. We should also add a unit test that runs canonical rerank pairs through new tokenizers and ensures rank order doesn't flip beyond a small threshold unless explicitly intended.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-16T03:12Z: promoted text-rerank-v2-2026-03-16 -> prod (jobs: runtime:canary->prod, tokenizer:patch-1). No errored steps.

anna_cs: Thanks everyone. I'll reply to the customer with repro confirmation and ETA for routing override. Action items: jordan create route override (P0), maria open regression bug (P0), raj add tokenizer_profile RFC (P1).
